data.title: Chainlink price prediction: How LINK can avoid a breakdown below $8
data.description:
Many of the large-cap crypto assets were deep in the red amid intense selling pressure in the past 24 hours. Chainlink [LINK] was one of the assets with the most bearish sentiment in the speculative markets.

At the time of writing, the Open Interest (OI) fell 11.6% in 24 hours alongside a 7.3% price slump as the The Funding Rates also retreated toward zero but were still positive.

The past month’s liquidation heatmap revealed a notable magnetic zone at $12 and another just under $13. These clusters of liquidity could attract LINK prices higher in the short term before a move lower.

In related news, Chainlink expanded access to Asian stock markets. This tokenization push has not bred new demand for the altcoin.

Examining Chainlink’s higher timeframe movement

The weekly chart revealed a swing level at $15 that the altcoin swept in September before falling lower. Another swing point at $10.87 was on the verge of being broken.

A weekly session close below this level would suggest a move toward $7.88, and $7 could be the next multi-week price leg.

As the liquidation heatmap showed, there was a smattering of liquidity around $10.30, which had a confluence with a recent weekly low of $10.27. Hence, a bullish short-term scenario would be a price sweep of $10.27 followed by a bounce past $11.80.

Chainlink bulls unable to overcome trendline resistance

For weeks now, Chainlink has seen a steady bearish trend sustained on the 4-hour timeframe. In particular, the month-long trendline resistance (orange) was a formidable opponent for buyers.

Additionally, it could be decision time for LINK. The $10.61 swing low from mid-September was under increasing pressure from the sellers, evidenced by the lower lows in recent weeks. Moreover, something has to give, and it is likely to be the buyers’ resolve.

Final Summary

  • Chainlink saw an 11.6% slide in Open Interest and a 7.3% price decline in 24 hours, making its short-term outlook among the most bearish in the top crypto assets.
  • The repeated challenge of the $10.6-$10.8 zone and steady selling pressure meant LINK could be headed towards $7.88 in the coming weeks.

data.title: Cardano Node 11.2 brings Dijkstra closer, but why did its price fall by 6%?
data.description:
Cardano [ADA] has an update coming soon. 

Node 11.2 is expected to hit mainnet by 8th November, and it will bring Dijkstra features with it.

Usually, a big release would give the price something to work with. Not this time though.

Cardano Node 11.2 pre-release lands, Leios saved for 11.3

Cardano Node 11.2 is out… only as a pre-release for now. The GitHub notes say it isn’t recommended for mainnet yet. The full release, likely tagged 11.2.1, is expected by the weekend (8th November).

The biggest change isn’t quite obvious though.

Node configs now come in a new “envelope” format; nodes older than 11.2 won’t be able to read them. Basically, this means operators will have to upgrade. The node’s API also got a boost. It can now run over a network address instead of only locally, and it picked up new tools for checking the mempool.

On the Dijkstra side, the CLI now handles sub-transactions. Dijkstra transactions can be submitted through the API too.

Leios is only groundwork here, and it’s switched off by default. The real thing is planned for Node 11.3, which is already being built.

Fair Min Fees will have to wait too.

Cardano dropped by 6.7% in a day, but…

… a $0.19 liquidity cluster is right above it.

The sell-off involved ADA falling from about $0.199 on 5th November to a low near $0.178 overnight.

The altcoin eventually clawed its way back to $0.186. However, at press time, it was still 6.7% below where it began.

The RSI on the short-term chart was at 48.3 too.

Additionally, the leverage has also taken multiple hits. Open Interest went down from about $197 million to $181 during the drop.

Funding seemed to be positive too with a reading of 0.0057%. This implied that longs haven’t given up yet.

Here’s what’s interesting, though. There appeared to be big pile of liquidations stacked on the heatmap, between $0.188 and $0.19. These seemed to be just above the press time trading price.

Prices cam often drift toward spots like that.

If Cardano pushes into that zone, those shorts could get squeezed… fast.

Final Summary

  • Cardano Node 11.2 is out as a pre-release; full mainnet release expected by weekend.
  • ADA fell by about 6.7%, with a liquidation cluster just above the price at press time.

data.title: Core Scientific plans to shut down Bitcoin mining despite Q3 revenue hitting $233M
data.description:
Core Scientific, once the largest Bitcoin [BTC] miner, has released its Q3 2026 report, but at the same time it has also announced its plans to completely exit Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026.

During its Q3 2026 earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard said the company expects to complete the mining wind-down in the fourth quarter and enter 2027 as a high-density colocation provider.

This decision came as the firm’s Q3 results were primarily driven by the expansion of its high-density colocation (HDC) business, which supports AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads.

Core Scientific’s AI shift

Remarking on the same, CEO Adam Sullivan said,

We are nearing full delivery under our first colocation agreement while construction under our second is underway across five campuses.

According to the reports, the company’s colocation revenue surged nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter to $215.4 million, compared to $136.7 million in Q2 2026 and $15 million in Q3 2025.

In fact, its total revenue also increased to $232.9 million, up from $164.2 million in the previous quarter and $81.1 million a year earlier.

As of the 30th of September, Core Scientific was billing for 485 megawatts (MW) of capacity, up from 395 MW in the previous quarter, representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation revenue.

Core Scientific’s Q3 2026 results

That said, the company also reported net income of $1.178 billion, compared to a net loss of $1.15 billion in Q2 2026 and $144 million in Q3 2025.

Meanwhile, adjusted EBITDA more than tripled quarter-over-quarter to $133.6 million, with its margin expanding to 57% from 25% in the previous quarter. Core Scientific’s gross profit also climbed to $123.3 million, compared to $70 million in Q2.

However, on the mining side, self-mining revenue declined to $12.3 million from $21.5 million in the previous quarter, while hosted mining revenue stood at $5.17 million. At the same time, revenue from hosting equipment for other Bitcoin miners also declined to $5.2 million from $8.7 million.

How it all began?

For those unaware, Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave, covering 590 MW of capacity, of which 485 MW was billable by September 2026. However, the transition also comes with challenges.

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in Q1 2026 amid weaker Bitcoin prices, low mining profitability, and declining equipment values. It also recorded a $41.9 million loss after terminating mining equipment agreements with Block and Proto in Q2.

That said, Core Scientific is not the only one, as, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin miners are increasingly selling BTC to fund operations while shifting their infrastructure towards AI and HPC.

Miner’s November performance analysis

This comes as miners swung from a huge inflow spike of about +7K BTC  in early 2026 to an outflow of about -5.7K BTC in early November, while the price slid from around $95K to $75.5K.

However, the latest netflow has settled back to a small positive reading of about 179.4 BTC, which suggests the miner selling pressure has cooled.

Final Summary

  • Q3 results were primarily driven by the expansion of its high-density colocation (HDC) business.
  • Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave.

data.title: Hyperliquid Strategies posts $620.6M Q3 profit – Mostly unrealized HYPE gains
data.description:
Hyperliquid Strategies Inc., the largest publicly traded HYPE treasury company, announced that its subsidiary has applied for registration as a US futures commission merchant (FCM).

CEO David Schamis said,

We deployed $802 million this quarter and filed an application to become a futures commission merchant. Those two moves are the same bet.

Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. reports quarterly financials

Hyperliquid was dominant in the part of on-chain finance that delivers real fees, and this value flows back to HYPE holders through systematic buybacks, the CEO added.

The company reported $620.6 million in quarterly profits. However, $803 million in unrealized gains came from its HYPE holdings, which totaled 38.9 million, with an average cost of $56.35 per token.

It raised $911 million in equity capital for the quarter ending on the 30th of September, spending $785 million to acquire 9.1 million HYPE tokens.

An FCM is a registered intermediary that holds customer funds and handles futures orders. The subsidiary would serve permissioned markets under HIP-3*, a planned upgrade whose regulatory approvals are pending.

If approved, Hyperliquid would get a regulated entry point for U.S. traders in the same week. There is no guaranteed timeline for the HIP-3*’s approval, the company stated.

Right now, the company’s stock, PURR, is highly correlated to HYPE token price swings.

Whales sell after billionaire Hyperliquid tweet pushes HYPE to local highs

On the 29th of October, billionaire American investor Stan Druckenmiller tweeted about Hyperliquid. Santiment Intelligence reported that this pushed the token price to local highs of $97.

Whale wallets were steadily selling their holdings during the rally. Four whales closed their longs entirely, banking around $5 million. The largest of these dumped $225k every five minutes when the price was around $95 and short-term sentiment was euphoric.

The weekly bullish structure extended from $51.13 to $97.99 (orange). The daily structure was also bullish, but the $75.17 swing low from September has been challenged once already.

The recent retreat from $97 revealed the sellers’ strength. A deeper drawdown below $75.17 remains likely. In that case, swing traders and investors should watch the $60.50-$68.35 demand zone.

Final Summary

  • The largest HYPE treasury company reported a $620.6 million profit for the latest completed quarter, mostly due to unrealized gains on HYPE holdings.
  • A subsidiary’s FCM application would serve permissioned markets under HIP-3*, which the company pitched to shareholders as regulated U.S. trader access to perpetual futures.

data.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80K – Why THESE signals threaten BTC’s price recovery
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] has reclaimed the $80,000 level, which is sitting above the 100-week Exponential Moving Average (EMA). This indicates a potential shift from short bearish control to bullish as long as BTC remains above the EMA.

The broader market is also green, with gains of about 2.38% on the day, with the total crypto capitalization approaching $2.70 trillion.

On the charts, Bitcoin is trading above a bull flag that had been in place since late September 2025. The EMA is also trading above the 0.50 Fibonacci retracement levels, a confirmation that BTC is entering the premium zone.

Still, buyers have yet to show real dominance over bears with the MACD faintly green.

Therefore, a breakdown to around $60,000 may be viable if bulls cannot keep the price above the EMA. The $60,000 level is aligned to 0.618 Fibonacci, a zone where most assets tend to bounce from.

Conversely, if bulls manage to sustain the strength, BTC could equal its all-time high of $126K, though $90,000 remains a significant supply zone. However, BTC is facing conflicting signals when on-chain data is explored.

Miner transfers and ETF outflows test buyer strength

Bitcoin miner, MARA Holdings, seems to be selling their Bitcoin holdings once again. The mining firm has moved 1,650 BTC worth over $132 million to Galaxy Digital, Copper, and other platforms.

Basically, Galaxy Digital received around 698 BTC valued at $56 million, while other platforms shared the remaining bounty from the Coinbase custody.

At the same time, U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs continued to see capital outflows over this week. For instance, in the past 24 hours, investors sold over $115 million in ETFs. This result took the weekly outflows to $990.98 million, less than $10 million away from hitting $1 billion.

This capital outflow from institutions puts bulls under a critical test of whether they can withstand this selling pressure.

The only way Bitcoin can hold its recovery above $80,000 is if buyers continue to long the token. At the same time, the selling pressure from the aforementioned institutions needs to stay in check, not outweighing the buyers’ volume.

Therefore, holding on to the new structure will be dependent on the behavior of market participants, including retailers, large investors, and institutions.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin reclaimed the $80,000 level, flipping the 100-week EMA into support, an indication of a potential shift to a long-term bullish structure. 
  • BTC was turning bullish on the weekly chart, but MARA’s dumping and Bitcoin ETF outflows tested its buyer strength.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs could surpass mutual funds in AUM by 2028: Bloomberg analyst
data.description:
As we are about to enter the third year of the Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETF being launched, it appears that BTC ETFs have a significantly stronger influence on BTC price returns than corporate Bitcoin accumulation.

According to the latest analysis by Ecoinometrics, an inflow of 10,000 BTC into spot Bitcoin ETFs corresponds to an estimated 3.2% boost in monthly Bitcoin returns. In comparison, the same amount of Bitcoin purchased by public companies contributes approximately 0.7% to monthly returns.

This suggests that ETF purchases have roughly 4.5 times the impact of corporate buying on Bitcoin’s price performance.

ETFs vs. AUM: The real winner

Adding more to this analysis, Bloomberg’s James Seyffart suggests that ETFs could surpass mutual funds in total Assets Under Management (AUM) within the next two to three years.

He said,

Their growth is only accelerating. If we stay on the same trend we’ve been on since the summer it will happen in ~two years.

Confirming his prediction, Syeffart used a chart and highlighted that ETFs accounted for 40.21% of total fund assets as of September 2026. And given the recent growth trends, ETFs could reach the 50% mark as early as September 2028 if the three-month growth rate continues.

However, other projections estimate this milestone between November 2028 and December 2029, depending on the period considered.

At the same time, ETFs rolling 12-month growth rate have also reached 3.74% in September 2026, above the historical average of 2.78% since the 2020 COVID market bottom. This indicates that ETF adoption is expanding faster than its long-term average.

Bitcoin ETF outflow streak continues

This comes as BTC ETFs are in their outflows streak. According to Farisde Investors data, from 1st to 5th November 2026, Bitcoin ETFs saw mostly outflows. In fact, so far in November, it has already recorded $869.82 million in outflows. The only exception being on the 4th of November, when the BTC ETFs recorded a net inflow of $74.6 million.

All of this happened as the price of BTC was trading at $76,102.46 after a drop of 52% in the past 24 hours.

That said, besides Bitcoin ETFs, Ethereum [ETH] ETFs also recorded $272.09  in outflows, and Binance [BNB] ETFs recorded $271.01K in outflows. Meanwhile, XRP ETFs were funded by $529.51K in outflows, Solana [SOL] ETFs had $1.18M in outflows, and Hyperliquid [HYPE] ETFs also saw $7.66 million in outflows.

In short, the pattern suggests risk-off sentiment across crypto at the start of November, and not just in Bitcoin. So, given the current data, it remains to be seen whether Seyffart’s predictions turn into reality or not.

Final Summary

  • ETF demand provides a more direct and consistent source of buying pressure in the spot market.
  • From 1st to 5th November 2026, Bitcoin ETFs saw mostly outflows with price action as dropping to $76K.

data.title: Bitcoin wipes out $731M as election hopes fade: BTC’s next test is…
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] traders faced liquidations on both sides as prices surged and then erased the rally.

On the 4th of November, Bitcoin climbed from $75.7k to $81.2k, triggering $407.92 million in liquidations. Shorts accounted for $309.98 million of that total.

The reversal on the 5th of November brought another $323.54 million in liquidations, including $294.11 million in longs. Meanwhile, total crypto Market Capitalization fell $132.7 billion that day, bringing losses since the local peak to $149 billion.

Short-term bullish sentiment following the midterm election results was immediately overrun by an equities market pullback, with major AI stocks coming under selling pressure.

Bitcoin volume trends show crypto isn’t exhausted, merely reactive

In a post on X, Glassnode observed that crypto traders are still here, despite the past month’s price retrace from $87k. Bitcoin [BTC] volume was at its lowest since 2023, before the August rally from $60k commenced.

Thereafter, volume remained above the August levels, which underlined sustained interest from traders and investors.

Rather than being a market collapse, the recent sell-off might be part of a healthy correction. Crypto intelligence platform Santiment posted that the crypto crowd became optimistic following the election results on the 4th of November.

This was a surprise, evidenced by the amount of short liquidations. Fueled by liquidations and FOMO, BTC briefly climbed past $81k.

Short-term FUD in reaction to selling in traditional markets across the globe sparked the Bitcoin reset. In both instances, the price went against the crowd’s expectations, showing why retail trader sentiment extremes can be counter-signals.

Bitcoin slips below key support level

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. wrote that the short liquidations reached the highest levels since late September. The Binance heist has also severely affected sentiment.

Since July, short-term holder BTC supply has expanded by 600k. It highlighted coins changing hands from long-term investors to newer market participants, and can also signal increased sensitivity to short-term price trends.

The True Market Mean was at $77.6k, and the brief foray above this level did not last. The metric measures the average cost basis of active investors while filtering out lost, dormant, or long-inactive coins.

A price slip below the TMM implied cooling market conditions and left investors at a loss on average. It could be a warning sign of a deeper correction.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin crowd expectations were punished over the past two days, leading to heavy liquidations and high volatility.
  • The volume trends were not comparable to the August slump, but losing the TMM suggested the market has reverted from bullish expansion to value-accumulation conditions.

data.title: Polygon eyes hard fork to recover $6.5 mln in stolen POL – But at what cost?
data.description:
In a surprising development, Polygon has proposed a major network upgrade to recover approximately 70.49 million POL tokens, worth around $6.5 million. These were those tokens that were stolen during two separate security incidents involving Polymarket and Binance in October 2026.

The proposal aims to move the stolen tokens from five attacker-controlled wallets into recovery wallets designated by the compromised companies.

Remarking on which the team noted,

5 attacker-controlled addresses hold about 70.49M POL: about 23.86M POL (4 addresses) from the Polymarket incident and about 46.63M POL (1 address) from the Binance incident. The funds cannot move, but nothing in the current setup lets them be returned either.

Things Polygon needs to do

Polygon’s block producers have already added these addresses to their transaction blocklists. This they did to prevent the attackers from moving the funds further. However, this measure only freezes the assets, and it does not return them to their actual owners.

The existing system also requires block producers to restart their infrastructure whenever blocklist changes are made, making it difficult to maintain these restrictions over time.

Hence, to address this issue, Polygon has proposed a hard fork, which is a major network upgrade that changes the blockchain’s underlying rules.

Under the proposal, at a predetermined block, the POL balances of the five identified wallets would be reduced to zero. The same amounts would then be credited to recovery addresses verified and designated by Polymarket and Binance.

However, for this plan to succeed, the proposal also requires both companies to prove ownership of their designated recovery addresses before the upgrade. If approved, developers will first implement and test the changes on Polygon’s Amoy testnet before deploying them on mainnet.

At the same time, validators, exchanges, and node operators will also need to upgrade their software before activation.
However, the proposal has raised important questions about decentralization and user ownership.

The red flag in question

Normally, blockchain transactions cannot be reversed or wallet balances moved without the owner’s private keys. But Polygon’s proposed intervention would override this principle through a consensus-level change.

However, the network argued,

It is an extreme action that should not be reproduced commonly.

This comes as the Polygon’s MATIC was trading at $0.098 after a hike of 2.08% in the past 24 hours.

But with 21Shares recently withdrawing approximately $11 million worth of POL from Coinbase over the past 30 days, including 45.7 million POL worth $4.08 million on 28th October, concerns remain.

Final Summary

  • As of now, Polygon’s block producers have already added these addresses to their transaction blocklists.
  • But at the same time, the proposal has also raised important questions about decentralization and user ownership.

data.title: PEARL integrates with NEAR Intents to expand cross-chain access for AI miners — Can demand follow?
data.description:
Pearl, the native token of the Pearl Layer-1 network, has launched on NEAR Intents. The move allows for swapping of tokens across more than 35 different networks. Additionally, the integration provides the Near Protocol’s [NEAR] Click API.

As a result, this makes it possible for wallets and applications to integrate Pearl [PEARL] token swaps.

In simple words, through NEAR’s infrastructure, miners will be able to swap PEARL for assets within all of those 35+ networks. Therefore, there may be easier access to stablecoins or other currencies for miners as they pay for electricity and hardware.

More importantly, Pearl’s Proof of Useful Work model links token issuance to AI computations that also secure the network. As such, miners receive both block rewards and inference fees based upon the same workload they are using to mine blocks.

This link could create a direct relationship between AI usage and token utility. However, for PEARL to have sustained value, it will require consistent AI-related workloads creating sufficient activity and generating fees that can support miners.

PEARL gains cross-chain access

As part of the integration, NEAR intents provides PEARL with access to an existing cross-chain market. No additional cross-chain bridges for each individual network would be required for this.

Currently, NEAR intents’ ecosystem provides a cross-chain marketplace that includes approximately 38 networks, along with more than 200 assets. Major stablecoin markets are included in the asset list as well.

This is important for miners who need to have liquid means to exit transactions quickly in order to meet costs associated with electricity and hardware. NEAR intents reported more than $37 billion in cumulative volume and more than $144 million in daily volume traded.

A large trading platform like this offers stability for those looking to utilize cross-chain swaps.

Moreover, confidential transactions enable users to transfer funds anonymously. Although the fact that the entire network is utilizing this function does not necessarily mean that there will be a greater demand for PEARL.

Instead, it will rely upon how frequently miners and traders utilize these services to conduct swaps, develop deeper liquidity levels, and ensure reliable execution.

Can AI demand sustain PEARL’s value?

PEARL’s next challenge is converting wider access into sustained market demand. PEARL’s market activity will show whether easier cross-chain access translates into genuine demand. At press time, the token was trading around $1.69, up 17% in the last 24 hours.

The daily volume increased alongside price rally, hovering near $12 million and was up 36%.

However, activity remains concentrated on a few centralized exchanges, suggesting NEAR access has yet to reshape its liquidity. This matters because GPU miners need reliable markets to convert rewards into operating funds.

Ultimately, stronger demand must therefore come from real AI workloads and paid inference, not token issuance alone.

Final Summary

data.title: ApeChain migrates to Chainlink CCIP for APE and USDC transfers – Details
data.description:
ApeChain is replacing LayerZero with Chainlink CCIP. This move comes as the layer 3 blockchain aims to strengthen its infrastructure and improve connectivity across the Yuga Labs ecosystem.

The migration makes CCIP the official cross-chain standard for ApeChain, Bored Ape Yacht Club applications, and APE.

Additionally, it will be migrating the ChainLink Cross-Chain Token (CCT) that is used by the CCT implementation of APE and USD Coin [USDC], among others. This is to enable programmable transfers from these tokens without having to use LayerZero’s former OFT.

Therefore, this may provide easier access to the decentralized application and community space across the Ethereum [ETH], Arbitrum, Base, and Polygon chains. As well, Chainlink has described CCIP as a single secure cross-chain standard.

Chainlink CCIP expands its reach

The expanded reach of Chainlink CCIP provides a larger scale significance for the ApeChain integration. Chainlink CCIP processes over $25 billion in cumulative transfer volume.

It also currently supports 60 to 77 different networks and has sent over 1.63 million messages. Previously, it was integrated with BitGo’s WBTC, Wyoming’s FRNT, and other assets from Kelp and Mantle.

These previous integrations have moved over $15 billion worth of token value via CCIP in 2026. In addition to providing additional support to this expanding network of users, Yuga Labs will also bring a large, consumer-focused, and NFT-centered ecosystem into play.

Ultimately, Rising transfers, repeat activity, deeper liquidity, and competitive fees will show whether adoption delivers lasting growth.

Can CCIP turn adoption into lasting demand?

While CCIP is continuing to expand its reach, it needs to continue translating this reach into sustainable revenue. More importantly, CCIP recently underwent its first upgrade (CCIP 2.0) since September 2026.

Additionally, integrations with Aave [AAVE], Lombard, and Venus demonstrate CCIP’s continued involvement in the development of DeFi. While CCIP continues to add to its involvement in DeFi infrastructure, commercial returns for the project remain limited.

This gap represents the difficulty in transitioning from simply being involved in infrastructure adoption into generating consistent economic returns.

Final Summary
